claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The starting microstructure contains a fine, homogeneous distribution of precipitates.
The starting state is free of significant oxide layers and internal voids.
An externally grown, compositionally selective Al- and Ti-rich protective oxide scale governs the elevated-temperature degradation rate.
An oxidizing atmosphere initially produces a coherent protective Al/Ti-rich oxide scale.
Continued oxide growth generates internal stress through growth mismatch and thermal-expansion mismatch with the FCC matrix.
Accumulated stress eventually causes the protective oxide scale to spall.
Scale spallation exposes fresh alloy to rapid oxidation.
Scale spallation creates localized stress concentrations that promote rapid mechanical failure.
Reducing conditions suppress formation of a coherent external protective oxide scale.
Under reducing conditions, oxygen penetrates the alloy and causes internal oxidation along grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary internal oxidation under reducing conditions produces voids.
Internal oxidation and void formation enhance creep and precipitate catastrophic failure.
Oxidizing exposure will produce an initially protective oxide layer followed by spallation and rapid loss of mechanical properties.
Reducing exposure will produce more uniform internal oxidation and void formation than the starting-state baseline.
Reducing exposure will significantly degrade creep resistance and tensile strength.
The proposed degradation behavior applies at temperatures of at least 800 degrees Celsius across oxidizing and reducing oxygen potentials.
Varying oxygen partial pressure while holding other thermal parameters constant is the controlled intervention proposed to reveal the governing degradation behavior.
The exact oxide composition, adherence, growth kinetics, and relative contributions of creep and oxidation damage are uncertain.
Failure to observe the predicted scale-spallation pathway in oxidizing gas or the predicted internal-oxidation and void pathway in reducing gas would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The tested range explicitly includes oxygen-poor reducing conditions, but the boundary statement characterizes the applicable domain as high-oxygen-potential regimes.
Internal oxidation is described as localized along grain boundaries in the mechanism but as more uniform in the predicted outcome; the intended spatial distribution is not resolved.
